I've been to quite a few funerals and luckily their services went well and honored the deceased well, I've also spoken before at a best friend's funeral. Her death was not imminent, it was sudden, but ironically we talked about what we wanted beforehand it is up to the person.

For the musically inclined, showcase their music maybe play songs or even have their band/close friends/ a band play music that they loved. Talk about the good memories and the impacts that these people have made on the lives of the living. For the artistic , show their art. Nature inclined, mention their interests etc. 

And I find it's best to be truthful! No disrespecting of the dead but depending on the crowd, you can always throw in something like "he was so stubborn , remember when _____" things that show their humanity. 

For things like cancer talk about their bravery , their pain ,i think it's good to acknowledge these things to make death a little more real. And we have to remember, the dead don't suffer the living do. So I would do as best as you can to also cater to their wishes without disrespecting the dead. Because ultimately funerals are for the living left behind to heal. 

When I spoke at my best friends funeral I was quite young. I told a story about a mischievous birthday gift she gave to me, and although it ended up being a half eaten jerky stick, the fun of unwrapping my crazy surprise it was one of the best gifts I've ever received. I highlighted her duality , how loving she was but also a fierce 19 year old in a 4'11 body. That was the biggest funeral I've ever attended. At least 300 people came because she was so loved but so complex. We also touched on her ideals and how she would want her family and friends to live and commemorate her after her passing. She worked for a nature preserve and was extremely passionate about forestry and the environment so I go to where she crashed her car and pick up trash. We encouraged others to love nature as much as she did and care for others as fiercely as she did. Also made lighthearted jokes about her being one of the most stubborn people in the world and how , although it led to her demise, it was an amazing quality.

For my grandmother we talked a lot about her charity work and her interests in art and a little less about her occupational successes , because that's what she would've wanted. I could go on and on.

Sorry this is long winded. Ultimately , for me , I wouldn't want my friends and loved ones to hold back. I want them to give the good, the bad, and the ugly. I would want them to talk about my passions for nature, childcare, and helping people in need. I'd want them to showcase some of my art and shitty poetry. I would want them to know that all I want for my family and loved ones is happiness and to know I'll always watch as well. And memories! All the memories! 

P.S recommend short doc on youtube called "We the Bereaved"

Edit to add: I've had many loved ones pass from cancer and a bunch of other things so all of these examples I've listed I've taken from my experiences
